newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures spent a relatively uneventful session following the fortunes of German bond futures to settle slightly higher in a market looking for a fresh impetus after the reversal of recent losses, traders said.

The June bond contract started strongly, building on early GLOBEX gains, but ran out of momentum above a key resistance level at 128.46/48 and drifted lower with Bunds, filling a gap left at the open.
After trading in a narrow range, French bonds got a late boost from Bunds, but tailed off into the close and traders said they expected further consolidation on Wednesday.
"The market was essentially a follower: we trailed the Bund when it fell back in the morning and we climbed with it when there was switching in favour of the Bund," one trader said.
Traders said there was little new money flowing into the cash market from domestic investors.

However one analyst said there had been a few large trades on behalf of domestic and overseas investors alike, moving further along the curve, based on the view the worst of the recent declines were over.
"They were lengthening the duration of their portfolios as they think the correction is over," he said.

Another analyst said investors were still unsure about putting new money into the long end of the French curve given the negative outlook for US long-bond yields but there was some interest in the TEC 10 variable rate OATs.
June PIBOR slipped slightly on Tuesday but outperformed Euromarks again, bringing the spread down to six basis points from a high for the year of 21 basis points.

Analysts said the short end in France was helped to a certain extent by the strength of the franc against the mark which was in turn prompting a minority to predict the Bank of France would cut the intervention rate on Thursday.

Others said the Bank of France would be unlikely to use up the 10 basis point margin between the intervention rate and the German repo rate too quickly and as long as the franc continued to move gradually towards its central parity, currency movements alone would not prompt a cut in rates.
The central bank's monetary policy council meets on Thursday.
The franc remained stable close to 46-month highs at 3.3648 against the mark.
